justifications.durability: The guard lives in product source and the covering test fails when its retirement is reverted - reproduced by this review in a scratch copy with the same failing id the manifest declares. The two cases drive the real crew.complete() entry point in an isolated RECKON_HOME, so the rule is exercised as production resolves it. The withdrawal is now made durable in observable state: the pointer is unlinked under _pointer_lock and the workspace released through _release_after_promotion, which reuses the gc classification so a worktree with uncommitted work would be withheld rather than removed. The endpoint of the first review's finding is removed. Residual weakness: the test asserts the pointer is gone but not that the workspace release actually ran, and the evidence fragment at docs/evidence/fragments/... is a stub carrying only a landing pointer with no evidence prose, so a regression that reported success without releasing the workspace would stay green.
justifications.evidence: Both named arms are present, complete and readable. Base e89a94bde 55 passed EXIT=0 (logs/base-arm-2.log); head 046c8ebaf 55 passed EXIT=0 (logs/head-arm-2.log); failure_count 0 in each, so the manifest's added_failure_count of 0 is well-founded. The declared negative control is genuine and this review reproduced it independently: removing pointer_path(run_id).unlink(missing_ok=True) from _complete_withdrawn_run reddens the pointer case (1 failed, 1 passed, EXIT=1; /tmp/reckon-crew-scratch/r-20261002T075029866672-review-of-a-withdrawn-run-completes-as-withdrawn/rev-negative-control.log). Deducted for the same provenance gap the first review recorded and which persists at the head arm: head-arm-2.log states the command with an unsubstituted <worktree> placeholder and omits the module_under_test and cwd header lines the base arm carries, so the head run's imported module path and working directory are not on the log itself; the reviewed run's manifest after_suite.command supplies the literal command, but the fact is not on the log the manifest points at.
justifications.fit: _complete_withdrawn_run sits immediately after _read_pointer_or_rebuild, the helper owner it belongs to, and is a private module-level helper returning a plain dict shaped like complete()'s other payloads, so the new outcome is one branch rather than a parallel refusal family. Its body mirrors the promotion tail (capture = _capture_member_session; release = _release_after_promotion then _retire_disposable_identity), so the withdrawal retires what a promotion retires. The docstring states the mechanism (a dispatch refused before a project is resolved leaves an empty project; there is no ledger to hold a row) rather than the incident. The single early-return call site sits inside complete(). No version suffixes, no plan or ticket identifiers in symbols, no author attribution. Ruff adds no findings: promotion.py carries the same three pre-existing findings at base and head and the same 13 format-diff hunks, and the new test file is clean (ruff check and format --check).
justifications.goal_fidelity: The fence's done-when - crew complete on a withdrawn run reports the withdrawal instead of failing project validation - is met at head 046c8ebaf. complete() (reckon/crew/promotion.py:4849-4853) reads the pointer or rebuilds it, and when the record names no project returns _complete_withdrawn_run (promotion.py:4684) before any ledger load or validation, so the pre-fix failure ('project "" must match ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$') no longer occurs. The payload is a parsed dict stating withdrawn true, status "withdrawn", project "", promoted false, ledger_row_written false, pointer_removed, a reason, and the surviving record. Both shapes the fence names are covered by tests/test_a_withdrawn_run_completes_as_withdrawn.py: a pointerless run rebuilt from its run directory (record carries rebuilt_from_run_directory true) and a surviving pointer that names no project. Head 046c8ebaf also closes the first review's follow-on (head dcd95ee5), which found the withdrawal reported but the pointer left live: the early return now unlinks the pointer and runs the same release/retire path a promotion uses (promotion.py:4703-4707), so the run no longer reads running forever after complete. That extra behaviour is within the node's declared write scope and the plan's section-10 goal (a run can always be reconciled from what survives).
justifications.scope_discipline: The base..head diff is confined to the node's declared write paths and nothing else: reckon/crew/promotion.py (+52), tests/test_a_withdrawn_run_completes_as_withdrawn.py (+96, new), docs/evidence/fragments/a-crew-process-ends-with-its-owner/a-withdrawn-run-completes-as-withdrawn.html (+23, new). git diff --name-only e89a94bde..046c8ebaf returns exactly those three paths. No plan HTML is edited (the fragment carries plan-verifies and leaves state to the coordinator), and the figures directory named in the manifest is not used, consistent with a done-when that names only the test artifact. git status in the reviewed worktree is clean at 046c8ebaf. commit 046c8ebaf is a second commit on the same node, retiring the pointer and workspace the first review flagged.
